title: Fees cap fails to ground Amex
full_text:
In a sign points-earning credit cards are far from dead, American Express is marking its 20-year partnership with Qantas by offering a 120,000 points sign-on bonus and new card artwork championing the airline.
The move follows an offer by Westpac for 150,000 bonus points and 50 status credits, and a similar deal offered by Qantas Money, provided that various terms and conditions are met.
Frequent flyer expert Adele Eliseo of The Champagne Mile said it was pleasing that some financial institutions were choosing a different approach to their competitors in the wake of the Reserve Bank-imposed cap on interchange fees.
Introduced on October 1, the changes reduce the revenue banks get from such fees, meaning they have less to spend on rewarding customers with airline points. As a result, some financial institutions have increased annual fees on co-branded cards, cut perks such as travel insurance cover and lounge passes, raised interest rates and lowered points earned per dollars spent.
Ms Eliseo said it was a wise move by American Express to lure customers wanting to switch providers as their card benefits were downgraded.
“It’s important to note that we are seeing a lot of multi-year bonuses effectively, which means points are awarded over several years, resulting in payment of more annual fees,” Ms Eliseo said. “That helps to guard against card churning, or people taking out a card for the bonus points, and then cancelling it relatively quickly. I think with the interchange caps, the card providers simply don’t have the budget anymore to be able to waste on people who aren’t going to be long-term customers.
“They’ve got to be careful about trying to market to the right people.” In the American Express Qantas Ultimate card offer, the 120,000 bonus points are delivered over two years – 70,000 in the first and 50,000 in the second, during which time the card holder has to stump up $900 in fees. However, it does come with the “sweetener” of a $450-a-year travel credit to spend on Qantas flights, Ms Eliseo said.
Qantas Loyalty chief executive Andrew Glance said members valued earning points on their everyday spending and more than 260,000 new points-earning cards were acquired in the year to June 30.
As a result, more than 35 per cent of all credit cards used in Australia earn frequent flyer points for the card holder. An estimated 4 per cent of those are co-branded American Express cards, which last year earned holders more than 10 billion points. Mr Glance said those points were used to book more than 500,000 flight redemptions in the year to June 30.
“With strong earn rates and premium travel benefits, the American Express card range remains a standout choice for members who want their daily spend to take them further,” Mr Glance said.
American Express Australia vice-president of co-brand, loyalty and partnerships Nick Alexander said the partnership with Qantas had gone from strength to strength over the past two decades. He said the new design would be introduced on co-branded Discovery, Ultimate and Premium cards for customers who loved to travel. “From uncapped Qantas points to lounge access and travel credits, they have consistently been a popular choice for our card members,” Mr Alexander said.
In a further sweetener for eligible customers, Qantas and American Express are giving away 20 holidays to Kangaroo Island in South Australia.
Existing or new card holders can enter by making a purchase on their co-branded card between now and the end of November.
Ms Eliseo said it was worth noting that American Express was not actually covered by the RBA’s interchange caps but had chosen to voluntarily participate. “They’re just considered a different network effectively, so they’re not covered by the determination,” she said. “There’s a discussion paper out now where they’re talking about covering Amex.”
